title: Contains Operator
description: Learn to check if a collection contains a specific element using the Contains operator.

data.text: The `Contains` operator checks whether a specified element exists in a collection and returns a boolean.
The `Contains()` extension method has two overloads:

data.title: Contains Method Signatures
data.code:
public static bool Contains<TSource>(this IEnumerable<TSource> source, TSource value);

public static bool Contains<TSource>(this IEnumerable<TSource> source, TSource value, IEqualityComparer<TSource> comparer);

data.title: Contains with Primitive Types
data.content: Checking if a value exists in a collection
data.code:
IList<int> intList = new List<int>() { 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 };
bool result = intList.Contains(10);  // returns false

data.text: For custom classes, `Contains` compares references by default, not values. This means it may return `false` even if an object with the same values exists:

data.title: Contains with Complex Types (Default)

data.text: To compare values of custom classes, implement `IEqualityComparer<T>`:

data.title: Contains with Custom Comparer
Not Supported in Query Syntax
data.text: The Contains operator is not supported in C# or VB.NET query syntax.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Contains checks if a collection contains a specific element
Compares values directly for primitive types
Requires IEqualityComparer<T> for value comparison of custom classes
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to learn about ElementAt and ElementAtOrDefault.
